title: Best AI Coding Tools June 2026: Updated After Fable 5 Changes Everything
description: Comprehensive analysis of how Fable 5's release on June 9, 2026 changed the AI coding tools landscape. Anthropic reports Fable 5 scored highest on Cognition's FrontierCode evaluation and was first to break 90% on core analytics benchmarks. GitHub Copilot now offers Fable 5 to Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise subscribers. The article provides detailed comparisons of Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cline, Codeium/Windsurf, and Amazon Q Developer, including pricing models and use case recommendations.
author: Developers Digest

title: U.S. Bars Foreigners From Using Anthropic's Most Advanced A.I. Models
description: The U.S. government ordered Anthropic to suspend access for all foreign nationals to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models, citing national security concerns. The order from the Commerce Department came after Anthropic unveiled Claude Mythos in April, which experts warned could become a powerful tool for hackers. The ban is highly unusual and could block even Anthropic employees who are citizens of allied nations from working on the technology.
author: Cade Metz and Dustin Volz (New York Times)

title: US orders Anthropic to disable AI models for all foreign nationals
description: The U.S. government ordered Anthropic to block access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals, including those working at Anthropic, citing national security concerns about the AI's capability to detect software vulnerabilities. The company received the directive at 5:21pm on Friday June 12 and had to cut off access abruptly. Anthropic noted that models from other providers like GPT-5.5 also possess similar code review capabilities.
author: Al Jazeera (citing Reuters)

title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
description: Anthropic received a US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for any foreign national due to national security concerns about a potential jailbreak technique. The government believes there's a method to bypass safeguards by asking the model to read codebases and fix software flaws. Anthropic noted this capability level is widely available from other models including GPT-5.5. Access was cut off at 6:59pm Pacific on June 12, 2026.
author: Simon Willison (citing Anthropic)

title: OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session, now with document context
description: Simon Willison updated his OpenAI WebRTC Audio playground tool to support the new GPT-Realtime-2 model (promoted as 'first voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning') and added the ability to paste document context for conversational exploration. The tool enables audio conversations in the browser about pasted documents.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
description: After two days with Claude Fable 5, Simon describes it as 'relentlessly proactive' - it knows many tricks and will deploy pretty much any of them to reach its goal. He shared his extensive experience with the model and noted how he had Fable 5 help with planning and GPT-5.5 xhigh in Codex Desktop for implementation to build a custom Datasette extras API explorer.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic Walks Back Policy That Could Have 'Sabotaged' AI Researchers Using Claude
description: Anthropic reversed their policy of invisible safeguards for frontier LLM development in Claude Fable/Mythos. The original policy would identify requests targeting frontier LML development and limit effectiveness without notifying users. Following huge outcry, Anthropic announced safeguards will now be visible, falling back to Opus 4.8 with visible notifications and refusal reasons.
author: Simon Willison (citing Wired and Anthropic)

title: Datasette Agent 0.2a0 with user interaction tools
description: New release of datasette-agent includes the ability for tools to ask users questions mid-execution. Tools can ask yes/no, multiple-choice, or free-text questions, suspending the agent turn until answered. The save_query tool allows agents to save SQL as Datasette stored queries with human approval. These features were enabled by a new LLM alpha built with Claude Fable 5.
author: Simon Willison

title: DiffusionGemma - Open weight 26B model from Google
description: Google released DiffusionGemma (google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it), an Apache 2 licensed open weight model. This continues research from the experimental Gemini Diffusion model. Simon tested it on NVIDIA's NIM cloud API and generated 2,409 tokens in 4.4 seconds (500+ tokens/second), demonstrating impressive performance for an open model.
author: Simon Willison

title: If Claude Fable stops helping you, you'll never know (Invisible safeguards controversy)
description: Jonathon Ready highlighted that Anthropic implemented invisible interventions in Fable 5/Mythos 5 that limit effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development (pretraining pipelines, distributed training infrastructure, ML accelerator design). Unlike cyber/bio safeguards, these would not be visible to users, using prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT instead. Simon noted this appears to be the first time Anthropic announced silent interventions. Update: Anthropic later walked back this policy.
author: Simon Willison (citing Jonathon Ready)

title: Initial impressions of Claude Fable 5
description: Simon spent 5.5 hours testing Claude Fable 5, describing it as a 'beast' - slow, expensive, but capable of churning through everything thrown at it. He noted the challenge is finding tasks it can't do, and shared extensive testing results and impressions.
author: Simon Willison

title: llm 0.32a3 - Almost entirely written by Claude Fable 5
description: New release of Simon's llm tool, with version 0.32a3 almost entirely written by Claude Fable 5. This demonstrates the increasing capability of AI coding agents to contribute meaningfully to real software projects.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy on Jevons Paradox and AI coding
description: Andrej Karpathy shared thoughts on how software increasingly comes 'out on a tap' with AI, triggering Jevons paradox where demand grows as capabilities increase. He noted you can ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke apps, expanded test suites, code optimization, custom research tools. This represents a fundamental shift in software development economics.
author: Andrej Karpathy (cited by Simon Willison)

title: Apple's 2026 WWDC AI Announcements - Skeptical View
description: Simon is holding to a strict 'I'll believe it when I see it' policy for Apple's WWDC AI announcements after being burned by unfulfilled 2024 promises. The new Siri AI features look feasible with today's technology, using a custom Gemini-derived model running on Private Cloud Compute. Apple will use vision LLMs to extract information from user screens. The Core AI library integrates with Meta's PyTorch ecosystem. Private Cloud Compute is running in Google Cloud using NVIDIA hardware while maintaining Apple's security protections.
author: Simon Willison
